content.title: Customer Service Representative Onboarding Plan - First 90 Days
content.summary: This plan outlines essential learning and compliance activities for the new Customer Service representative. It includes mandatory tasks such as handbook acknowledgement, emergency absence reporting, and readiness review, as well as optional tasks like archive review to improve record management.

items.source_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
items.learning_objective: Recognize the obligation to acknowledge the employee handbook immediately upon joining, understanding the process if digital access is unavailable.
items.practical_activity: Simulate receiving the employee handbook, and complete an acknowledgement form either digitally or on paper, depending on the scenario provided by the trainer.
items.lesson: All employees must acknowledge receipt and understanding of the current employee handbook within 1 working day of joining. If you cannot access the digital handbook, HR will note the access issue and arrange for you to complete a supervised paper acknowledgement within this same timeframe. This process ensures you are informed about company policies and procedures early in your employment.
checklist: Locate the latest version of the employee handbook.
Acknowledge the handbook receipt digitally or on paper if digital access is unavailable.
Notify HR immediately if handbook access is not possible.
Complete supervised paper acknowledgement if required.

scenario.prompt: You just joined as a Customer Service representative but cannot access the digital employee handbook due to a system outage. What steps do you take to comply with the handbook acknowledgement requirement?
scenario.expected_response: I notify HR about the system outage as soon as possible. HR will record the outage and arrange for me to sign a supervised paper acknowledgement of the handbook within the 1 working day period.

quiz.question: What must an employee do if they cannot access the digital employee handbook within one working day of joining?
options: Notify HR who will record the outage and arrange a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
Delay acknowledging the handbook until access is restored.
Ignore the handbook acknowledgement requirement if access is unavailable.
Request an extended deadline for handbook acknowledgement.
quiz.explanation: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

rubric.criterion: Scenario response explains notifying HR and completing a paper acknowledgment
Practical activity shows handbook acknowledgement completion per process
Checklist steps are accurately followed

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to notify management quickly during emergencies preventing attendance, and recognize the role of HR and nominated contacts if direct communication is not possible.
items.practical_activity: Role-play a scenario where you or a designated contact report an emergency absence to the manager and HR, documenting the circumstances accurately.
items.lesson: Employees must notify their manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents them from attending work. If the employee cannot personally communicate, HR will accept notification from a nominated contact and must document the situation. Prompt communication ensures appropriate coverage and support during unforeseen absences.
checklist: Identify your manager's contact information for emergency notification.
Notify your manager immediately in case of emergency preventing attendance.
If unable to notify yourself, ensure a nominated contact informs HR.
Confirm HR records the circumstances reported by the nominated contact.

scenario.prompt: You are suddenly hospitalized and cannot notify your manager about your absence. What happens next according to the policy?
scenario.expected_response: My nominated contact contacts HR to notify them about my emergency absence, and HR records the circumstances as required.

quiz.question: If an employee cannot notify their manager of an emergency absence, what is HR's role?
options: HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
HR ignores notifications unless from the employee.
HR contacts the employee repeatedly until they respond.
HR waits for the employee to return to work before recording anything.
quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

rubric.criterion: Scenario response shows understanding of emergency notification procedure
Practical activity demonstrates correct notification from a nominated contact
Checklist compliance with notification protocol and recording

items.source_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
items.learning_objective: Recognize the requirement for managers to assess employee readiness within the first 30 days and document any training needs or limits on supervised work.
items.practical_activity: Prepare a self-assessment report identifying your skills, gaps, and areas where supervision is needed to assist your manager's readiness review.
items.lesson: Managers are required to review each employee's readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days of employment. This review documents any gaps in skills, limits on the type or amount of supervised work the employee can perform, and schedules follow-up dates to monitor progress. This process ensures proper support and success in your new role.
checklist: Complete a self-assessment of your skills and training gaps.
Discuss your readiness and supervised-work limits with your manager.
Attend the readiness review meeting within the first 30 days.
Follow up on the documented plans and dates as agreed.

scenario.prompt: Your manager asks you to prepare for your readiness review within your first month. What information do you provide and why?
scenario.expected_response: I provide a self-assessment of my skills, identify any gaps or areas where I need supervision, so my manager can document these and plan follow-up to support my development.

quiz.question: What must managers document during the employee readiness review within the first 30 days?
options: Remaining gaps, supervised-work limits, and follow-up dates.
Only employee strengths and achievements.
Attendance records and punctuality.
Completed training courses only.
quiz.explanation: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
quiz.evidence_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

rubric.criterion: Scenario response includes self-assessment and training gap identification
Practical activity demonstrates preparation for readiness review
Checklist displays adherence to readiness review steps

items.source_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
items.learning_objective: Encourage employees to evaluate record archive naming and indexing for improved searchability and propose enhancements.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a mock quarterly archive review session and submit suggestions for improving naming conventions or indexing based on your findings.
items.lesson: Employees who manage records are encouraged, though not required, to review the searchability of archived records quarterly. This review helps identify ways to improve the naming or indexing systems, making retrieval more efficient. Regular proposals for enhancements keep the archives organized and accessible.
checklist: Familiarize yourself with current archive naming and indexing standards.
Perform a review of archive searchability as if it were quarterly.
Document findings and propose improvements for naming or indexing.
Share suggestions with the records management team.

scenario.prompt: During your first month, you are asked to review the archives. What should you focus on and what should you do with your observations?
scenario.expected_response: I focus on how easily records can be found using the current naming or indexing system, then I document any issues and propose improvements to help make searching more efficient.

quiz.question: What are record owners encouraged to do quarterly to improve archives?
options: Review archive searchability and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
Delete old records to save space.
Ignore archive structure changes to maintain consistency.
Only update records without reviewing searchability.
quiz.explanation: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

rubric.criterion: Scenario response identifies focus on searchability and proposes improvements
Practical activity delivers realistic improvement proposals
Checklist confirms completion of review and communication steps

items.source_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to properly store operational evidence to comply with company policy and maintain accurate records.
items.practical_activity: Simulate storing a sample operational document into the approved case repository and verify no local copies are sole records.
items.lesson: Proper documentation is crucial for operational transparency and audit readiness. Employees must always store evidence—such as decisions or transaction records—in the company's approved case or document repository. Relying only on local copies is prohibited because it risks losing the official record. Using the designated repository ensures records are accessible and secure, supporting accountability and compliance.
checklist: Identify the correct approved repository for storing operational evidence.
Upload a document into the repository following security guidelines.
Confirm no local copies are the sole record of any transaction or decision.
Verify document accessibility in the repository for authorized personnel.

scenario.prompt: You have just completed a customer transaction and saved a summary on your local desktop. How do you ensure compliance with the document storage policy?
scenario.expected_response: I will upload the transaction summary to the approved case repository and ensure the local file is not the only copy. This guarantees the record is official and accessible.

quiz.question: According to company policy, where must operational evidence be stored?
options: In the approved case or document repository only
On the employee's local computer as the sole copy
Both local copy and email to manager
Any personal cloud storage accessible to the team
quiz.explanation: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies and uses the approved case repository
Avoids having a local copy as sole record
Completes the practical upload accurately

items.source_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
items.learning_objective: Learn steps to take when an unintended data transfer occurs, including reporting and preserving evidence.
items.practical_activity: Review a simulated accidental disclosure event; identify immediate actions and draft a report following POL-09 procedures.
items.lesson: When a suspected accidental disclosure happens, employees must act quickly to stop any unintended transfer if possible. They are required to report the incident immediately through the POL-09 procedure. Preserving all evidence related to the incident is mandatory, and it is prohibited to conceal or silently delete the incident history. Prompt reporting protects the company and supports incident resolution and compliance.
checklist: Attempt to stop the unintended information transfer immediately.
Report the suspected disclosure promptly via POL-09.
Preserve all evidence relating to the incident.
Do not delete or conceal any incident history records.

scenario.prompt: You accidentally emailed sensitive client information to the wrong recipient. What should you do next?
scenario.expected_response: I would immediately try to recall or stop the email if possible, then report the incident through POL-09 right away, preserving all evidence and not deleting any related history.

quiz.question: If you suspect an accidental data disclosure, what is your required action?
options: Stop the transfer if possible and report immediately through POL-09
Ignore if it seems minor and delete the incident history
Report only if you are sure the data was viewed
Wait for management to discover the issue before acting
quiz.explanation: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

rubric.criterion: Effectively attempts to stop unintended transfer
Completes immediate and accurate incident report
Preserves evidence and does not delete history

items.source_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
items.learning_objective: Demonstrate respectful communication and understand proper channels for reporting concerns about harassment, threats, or discrimination.
items.practical_activity: Role-play responding to scenarios involving disrespectful communication and practice reporting concerns confidentially through HR.
items.lesson: Respectful communication in the workplace is mandatory. Employees must avoid harassment, threats, or discrimination towards others. If someone witnesses such behavior, they should report their concerns discreetly through the confidential HR channel and avoid discussing allegations with colleagues to protect privacy and integrity. This promotes a safe, inclusive, and professional work environment.
checklist: Communicate with coworkers respectfully at all times.
Do not engage in harassment, threats, or discrimination.
If witnessing concerns, report confidentially through HR.
Avoid sharing allegations or discussing concerns with other employees.

scenario.prompt: You overhear a colleague making discriminatory comments about another employee. How should you respond?
scenario.expected_response: I should report the incident confidentially through the HR channel without spreading the information to other coworkers.

quiz.question: If you witness harassment, what is the correct way to report it?
options: Report discreetly through confidential HR channels without sharing with colleagues
Discuss the incident openly with your team first
Ignore it if you are not directly involved
Email all employees about the behavior
quiz.explanation: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

rubric.criterion: Demonstrates respectful communication behaviors
Accurately reports concerns through correct confidential channel
Maintains confidentiality by not spreading allegations

items.source_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
items.learning_objective: Achieve proficiency by scoring at least 80% on required assessments and understand the retake procedure upon failure.
items.practical_activity: Complete a practice knowledge assessment and review incorrect answers to prepare for the official assessment.
items.lesson: To ensure employee competence, all mandatory knowledge assessments must be passed with a minimum score of 80 percent. If an employee fails an attempt, they must undertake targeted study to address the gaps before retaking the assessment. Importantly, the score from the original failed attempt must remain recorded for compliance tracking and improvement purposes.
checklist: Complete the mandatory knowledge assessment.
Score at least 80 percent to pass.
If unsuccessful, review missed topics carefully.
Retake the assessment after targeted revision.
Ensure all assessment attempts are documented.

scenario.prompt: You scored 75% on your first knowledge assessment attempt. What are the next steps?
scenario.expected_response: I must study the areas I missed, then retake the assessment. My original 75% score will stay recorded.

quiz.question: What must an employee do if they fail the mandatory knowledge assessment?
options: Undertake targeted revision and then attempt the assessment again; the original attempt score remains recorded
Ignore the result and continue working without retaking
Retake the assessment immediately without revision
Delete the original result and retake to try for a better score
quiz.explanation: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

rubric.criterion: Passes assessment with minimum 80%
Completes targeted revision before retake if failed
Understands and complies with result recording requirements

items.source_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
items.learning_objective: Learn to correctly identify and request correction of attendance inaccuracies within the required timeframe while understanding HR's retention responsibilities.
items.practical_activity: Review a simulated attendance record with an error and submit a correction request within a simulated system, documenting the original value and supporting evidence.
items.lesson: Employees are required to request correction of any inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering the issue. This quick action helps maintain accurate attendance records. Additionally, Human Resources retains the original attendance value along with all evidence supporting the correction for audit and verification purposes. Prompt reporting ensures compliance and record integrity in the company’s attendance system.
checklist: Identify inaccuracies in attendance entries promptly.
Submit a correction request within 2 working days of discovery.
Ensure original attendance values and correction evidence are documented.
Communicate with HR as required regarding attendance corrections.

scenario.prompt: You notice that your recorded clock-out time for yesterday is incorrect in the attendance system. What steps should you take?
scenario.expected_response: I will submit a correction request within 2 working days of discovering the error and provide any evidence supporting the correction. I understand that HR will keep the original value and documentation for records.

quiz.question: Within what timeframe must employees request correction for an inaccurate attendance entry?
options: Within 2 working days of discovering it
Within 5 calendar days of the recorded entry
Within 1 working week after noticing it
quiz.explanation: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

rubric.criterion: Explains the correction request timeframe accurately
Demonstrates understanding of HR's record retention
Completes practical correction request within scenario parameters

items.source_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to identify and use the correct document versions and manage revision history during activities.
items.practical_activity: Simulate retrieving and using the correct document version for a customer interaction based on the activity date and noting revision links and changes.
items.lesson: Document owners are responsible for linking each new document revision to the superseded version and clearly identifying which sections have changed. Employees must use the document version effective on the date of their business activity to avoid errors. Historical document versions remain available for audit purposes to track changes over time and ensure transparency in documentation practices.
checklist: Verify the effective date of documents before use.
Check links to superseded document versions.
Note and understand all identified changed sections.
Retain knowledge of historical copies for audit references.

scenario.prompt: A client inquiry references a policy updated last week. How do you ensure you use the correct document version for your response?
scenario.expected_response: I check the effective date of the document to confirm it was valid on the inquiry date, ensure I review the changes linked to the previous version, and use this current version for my response, keeping historical versions accessible if needed.

quiz.question: What must employees use to ensure policy compliance during activities?
options: The document version effective on the date of the activity
The latest document version regardless of activity date
The oldest available document version for consistency
quiz.explanation: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
quiz.evidence_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies the effective document version
Explains the importance of revision linking and change identification
Completes practical activity using correct document version

items.source_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
items.learning_objective: Understand the roles in incident management including appointment of a lead and coordination responsibilities.
items.practical_activity: Simulate an incident handover where you document appointment of the incident lead and outline their coordination tasks alongside IT's technical role.
items.lesson: When an incident occurs, the duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and formally record the handover to ensure clear ownership. The IT team lead handles technical containment, while the incident lead manages business decisions and oversees communication with stakeholders. This delineation ensures prompt, effective management and resolution of incidents.
checklist: Confirm appointment of an incident lead by the Operations Manager.
Record details of the handover accurately.
Understand IT lead's role in technical containment.
Recognize incident lead’s responsibility for business decisions and communication.

scenario.prompt: An operational issue arises. What steps should the Operations Manager take regarding incident management?
scenario.expected_response: The Operations Manager should appoint an incident lead and record the handover. While IT leads technical containment, the incident lead will coordinate business decisions and communications.

quiz.question: Who coordinates business decisions and communication during an incident?
options: The incident lead appointed by the Operations Manager
The IT lead responsible for technical containment
The Operations Manager without delegation
quiz.explanation: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
quiz.evidence_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the correct roles and responsibilities in incident management
Accurately documents the incident lead appointment and handover
Completes practical scenario showing understanding of coordination roles

items.source_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
items.learning_objective: Learn to properly delete approved temporary exports of customer data within the specified timeframe unless a preservation hold applies.
items.practical_activity: Practice identifying when a temporary data export must be deleted, and simulate applying a preservation hold to postpone deletion if applicable.
items.lesson: Employees are required to delete any approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task has ended. This timely removal helps protect customer data privacy. However, if there is a documented preservation hold, deletion must be suspended, but only for those specific records identified in that hold. This ensures compliance with data retention policies and legal holds.
checklist: Identify the end of the approved export task.
Delete temporary customer-data exports within 24 hours after task completion.
Recognize and respect documented preservation holds.
Suspend deletion only for records specified in the preservation hold.

scenario.prompt: You have just completed a task requiring a temporary export of customer data. What must you do regarding the data export?
scenario.expected_response: I must delete the temporary customer-data export within 24 hours after the task ends unless there is a documented preservation hold for specific records, which means I suspend deletion only for those records.

quiz.question: Within what timeframe must temporary customer-data exports be deleted after an approved task ends?
options: Within 24 elapsed hours
Within 48 working hours
Within 7 calendar days
quiz.explanation: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

rubric.criterion: Explains deletion timeframe accurately
Demonstrates understanding of preservation hold exceptions
Completes practical deletion or hold application within scenario

items.source_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
items.learning_objective: Understand and complete prerequisite training before performing any restricted tasks independently as a CS employee.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a manager scheduling and documenting a supervised practice session without marking the prerequisite training complete. Prepare a checklist to verify completion of prerequisite training before task performance.
items.lesson: Employees must complete all required prerequisite training before they perform any restricted tasks independently. While a manager can arrange supervised practice to help you gain experience, they are not allowed to mark your prerequisite training as complete until you have actually completed it. This ensures that you are fully prepared and qualified before handling sensitive or restricted activities on your own.
checklist: Identify relevant prerequisite trainings for your role
Verify completion of prerequisite training before any restricted task
Request supervised practice if needed before independent work
Ensure no unmet prerequisite is marked complete by managers

scenario.prompt: You have not completed the prerequisite training for a restricted task but your manager offers supervised practice and asks you to start independently.
scenario.expected_response: Explain to your manager that you cannot start performing the task independently until you have completed the prerequisite training, though you can participate in supervised practice sessions.

quiz.question: What must an employee do before independently performing restricted tasks?
options: Complete relevant prerequisite training
Start supervised practice sessions immediately
Have the manager mark training as complete before practice
Perform the task and learn on the job
quiz.explanation: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

rubric.criterion: Clearly states prerequisite training must be completed before independent work
Explains manager's role in arranging but not completing training
Demonstrates appropriate checklist and practical activity

items.source_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
items.learning_objective: Learn to assess parcel weight and route accurately and request assistance when required, adhering to safety limits.
items.practical_activity: Practice weighing simulated parcels and determining the correct handling route. Identify when to request approved assistance based on posted safe-handling limits, avoiding assumptions about weight limits.
items.lesson: Before lifting any parcel, you must assess both its weight and the route for delivery. If the parcel’s weight exceeds the posted safe-handling limit, you must request approved handling assistance. Importantly, you cannot create or assume a universal weight limit; each task requires an assessment based on the posted safe-handling instructions. This protects your safety and ensures compliance with company policies.
checklist: Check parcel weight accurately
Evaluate the delivery route for obstacles
Compare weight against posted safe-handling limits
Request approved handling assistance if limit exceeded

scenario.prompt: You find a parcel heavier than usual but no posted universal weight limit is displayed. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Assess the parcel's weight and route carefully and then request approved handling assistance if it exceeds the posted safe-handling limit, not inventing a universal limit.

quiz.question: What should you do if a parcel exceeds the posted safe-handling limit?
options: Request approved handling assistance
Lift the parcel yourself carefully
Ignore weight and focus on delivery speed
Invent a universal weight limit for all parcels
quiz.explanation: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

rubric.criterion: Accurately assesses parcel weight and route in scenario
Correctly requests approved assistance when needed
Demonstrates understanding in practical activity

items.source_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
items.learning_objective: Show proficiency in critical role task steps to an authorized assessor before working independently.
items.practical_activity: Perform a simulated role task including all safety and privacy critical steps and present it to an authorized assessor for evaluation.
items.lesson: Before you can work independently in your role, you must demonstrate all critical steps of your tasks to an authorized assessor. This means showing you can perform safety and privacy-related actions properly. A numerical score alone cannot compensate if you fail to execute any critical safety or privacy step. This ensures your work meets necessary standards to protect customers and yourself.
checklist: Identify critical safety and privacy steps for your tasks
Practice performing every critical step accurately
Schedule demonstration with authorized assessor
Complete demonstration successfully before independent work

scenario.prompt: You fail to perform a privacy step during a role task demonstration. What is the outcome?
scenario.expected_response: You cannot proceed to independent work despite your general scores; you must repeat and correctly perform all safety and privacy critical steps.

quiz.question: What happens if you fail a safety or privacy critical step during your demonstration?
options: You must repeat the step; a numerical score cannot compensate
You pass if overall score is high
You ignore the step and proceed
Your manager can approve you regardless
quiz.explanation: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies and performs all critical steps
Understands importance of safety and privacy steps
Demonstrates practical competence in activity

items.source_quote: The Customer Support Executive must record the resolution, supporting evidence and customer notification before closure. Lack of customer response alone must not be recorded as successful delivery.
items.learning_objective: Learn to properly record resolution details, evidence, and customer notification before closing support cases.
items.practical_activity: Review sample case files and update them with resolution records, evidence, and documented customer notification. Detect and correct improper closures based solely on lack of response.
items.lesson: As a Customer Support Executive, you must record the resolution of each customer issue, include supporting evidence, and document notification to the customer before you can close the case. Simply noting a lack of customer response does not count as successful delivery or closure. Ensuring all these elements are properly recorded safeguards customer experience quality and company standards.
checklist: Record final resolution details
Attach or reference supporting evidence
Document customer notification
Verify closure is not based only on lack of response

scenario.prompt: You want to close a case but the customer hasn’t responded after multiple contacts. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: You should not close the case solely due to lack of response. Record the resolution, supporting evidence, and proof of notification before closing.

quiz.question: What must a Customer Support Executive do before closing a case?
options: Record resolution, supporting evidence, and customer notification
Close the case if the customer does not respond
Record only the resolution details
Notify the customer after closure
quiz.explanation: The Customer Support Executive must record the resolution, supporting evidence and customer notification before closure. Lack of customer response alone must not be recorded as successful delivery.
quiz.evidence_quote: The Customer Support Executive must record the resolution, supporting evidence and customer notification before closure. Lack of customer response alone must not be recorded as successful delivery.

rubric.criterion: Completes case records with resolution, evidence, and notification
Demonstrates understanding of closure requirements in scenario
Correctly updates sample case files in activity

items.source_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
items.module_title: Recipient Verification: Protecting Customer Shipment Information
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply the approved workflow to verify requesters before releasing shipment recipient details, ensuring customer privacy.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a customer call requesting shipment information with only a shipment number provided and practice following the approved verification workflow before disclosing any recipient details.
items.lesson: It is essential to verify the identity of anyone requesting shipment details to protect customer privacy and comply with data protection policies. Employees must follow the approved verification workflow before disclosing any shipment recipient address or contact information. Simply having the shipment number does not grant authorization to share these sensitive details. This ensures that shipment information is only released to properly verified and authorized requesters, safeguarding both the customer and the company.
checklist: Familiarize with the approved requester verification workflow.
Do not disclose recipient address or contact details when only a shipment number is provided.
Confirm requester identity through required verification steps before providing shipment information.
Document verification steps taken during the inquiry.

scenario.prompt: A caller requests the recipient address for shipment #12345 but does not provide any additional verification information. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: I would politely inform the caller that I cannot provide recipient address details based on the shipment number alone and proceed through the approved verification workflow to confirm their authorization before any disclosure.

quiz.question: According to the policy, when is it acceptable to disclose shipment recipient address or contact details?

items.learning_objective: Learn the requirements for device usage and data protection when accessing restricted company data.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a checklist-based review of your device profile to verify it is company-managed or explicitly approved, and simulate inspecting file storage permissions.
items.lesson: To protect sensitive company information, employees are required to access restricted data only through company-managed devices or devices with an explicitly approved profile. Additionally, company files must never be stored or transferred to personal storage services, which could pose risks of unauthorized access. This ensures compliance with data protection policies and safeguards customer information.

Confirm you do not use personal storage services for company files.
Understand why restricted data access must be controlled.
Know how to report unauthorized data access attempts.

scenario.expected_response: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data and must not store company files on personal storage services.

options: Use only company-managed or explicitly approved devices; personal storage for company files is prohibited.
Any personal device can be used if password protected.

quiz.explanation: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.

Transfer escalation contacts clearly.

items.source_quote: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
items.learning_objective: By the end of this module, you will be able to create clear and accurate incident records that include all required details while properly labeling speculation and excluding sensitive credentials.
items.practical_activity: Create a sample incident record from a simulated incident scenario including observed facts, discovery time, affected services, and initial actions. Label speculative information and ensure no credentials are included.
items.lesson: When responding to an incident, it is essential that the first available responder promptly creates a detailed incident record. This record must contain observed facts — not assumptions — the time the incident was discovered, which services are affected, and any initial actions taken. If there is any speculation about the incident, it must be clearly labeled to avoid confusion later. Personal or system credentials must never be included in the incident record to protect privacy and security. Maintaining accurate records ensures quick and coordinated responses.
checklist: Identify and document observed facts of the incident
Record the exact discovery time
List all affected services accurately
Describe initial actions taken
Label any speculative information clearly
Exclude any credentials or sensitive data

scenario.prompt: You are the first responder to a service outage affecting the payment system. You observe the service is down and a colleague suggests it might be due to a recent update, but you are not sure yet.
scenario.expected_response: You document the observed fact that the payment system is down and record the discovery time. You list the payment service as affected and note any initial troubleshooting steps you performed. You include your colleague's suggestion as speculation, clearly labeled as such, and ensure no passwords or credentials are recorded.

quiz.question: What must the first available responder include in an incident record?
options: Observed facts, discovery time, affected services, initial actions; label speculation; exclude credentials
Only the impacted services and estimated recovery time
All possible causes including speculation, and any credentials needed
Just the initial actions taken without time details
quiz.explanation: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
quiz.evidence_quote: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.

rubric.criterion: Completeness of incident record details
Correct labeling of speculation and exclusion of credentials

items.source_quote: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.

items.learning_objective: You will learn how to properly issue internal status checkpoints every 30 minutes during continuity events, including the required contents of each checkpoint update.

This involves issuing status checkpoints at least every 30 elapsed minutes until the services return to normal. Each checkpoint must clearly state the current impact of the outage, identify the owner responsible for addressing the issue, and specify when the next update will be provided. Regular checkpoints ensure transparency and coordination during incidents.

Issue status update every 30 minutes at minimum
Include current impact details in each update
Name the owner responsible for resolution
Specify the next update time clearly

quiz.question: What information is required in each outage checkpoint during a continuity event?
options: Current impact, owner, next update time

quiz.explanation: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.

items.source_quote: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to amend records correctly by documenting the author, time, and reason without overwriting original values.

quiz.question: How must record errors be corrected?

By deleting incorrect entries and re-entering data
By overwriting original values silently to avoid confusion

quiz.explanation: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.

Protecting account credentials reduces risk of unauthorized access and keeps sensitive data safe.

Never share your password or authentication codes with anyone.

Avoid using service accounts for routine interactive tasks.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies the prohibition on password sharing in response.

Completes practical activity by verifying personal account use and security.

items.source_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
items.learning_objective: Understand the hierarchy of company guidance documents and proper resolution of conflicting instructions.
items.practical_activity: Locate the latest approved policy, applicable SOP, role guide, and FAQ for your role. Practice determining which document to follow when instructions differ.
items.lesson: When performing your duties, always follow the most authoritative and current documents in order of precedence: start with the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), followed by an approved role guide, and lastly any FAQ. Lower-authority documents cannot override policies. If you encounter conflicting instructions that cannot be resolved, you must escalate the issue to the policy owner for clarification before proceeding. This ensures consistent and compliant operations.
checklist: Identify and access the latest approved policy relevant to your role.
Review the applicable SOP for your tasks.
Consult your approved role guide for role-specific instructions.
Check FAQs only after consulting the above guidance.
Escalate unresolved document conflicts to the policy owner.

scenario.prompt: You find that a recent FAQ conflicts with an existing approved policy about handling customer data. What is the correct course of action?
scenario.expected_response: Follow the approved policy as it has higher authority; escalate the conflict to the policy owner for resolution before proceeding.

quiz.question: If you find conflicting instructions between a policy and a FAQ, which should you follow?
options: The policy, and escalate the conflict to the policy owner.
The FAQ, since it is more practical.
Both equally; use your judgment.
Ignore both and ask a colleague.
quiz.explanation: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies that policy overrides FAQ in conflicts.
Demonstrates proper escalation of unresolved conflicts.
Successfully completes document review and prioritization activity.

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
items.learning_objective: Learn to promptly notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 minutes of a critical incident and apply immediate emergency actions without delay.
items.practical_activity: Given a simulated critical incident, practice notifying the duty Operations Manager within 15 minutes and documenting the notification promptly afterward.
items.lesson: When you discover a critical incident, you must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes to ensure timely escalation and response. Do not wait to create or wait for a ticket before taking immediate emergency or containment actions; these must begin right away to mitigate impact. After taking urgent action, submit a notification record as soon as practical to document the incident and your response. This protocol helps maintain system safety and operational continuity.
checklist: Immediately recognize signs of a critical incident.
Notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 minutes of discovery.
Start emergency or containment actions without waiting for a ticket.
File the notification record promptly after initial response.

scenario.prompt: You identify a critical incident affecting customer service systems at 2:00pm. When and how should you escalate?
scenario.expected_response: Notify the duty Operations Manager by 2:15pm and immediately begin containment actions without waiting for ticket creation; document notification promptly afterward.

quiz.question: What is the maximum time allowed to notify the duty Operations Manager after discovering a critical incident?
options: 15 elapsed minutes
30 minutes
1 hour
Immediately with no time limit
quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.

rubric.criterion: Timely notification within 15 minutes in scenario.
Effective demonstration of immediate containment actions.
Accurate and prompt documentation of notification.

matrix_snapshot.title: Unexpected absence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

matrix_snapshot.title: Archive review
matrix_snapshot.text: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

matrix_snapshot.title: Handbook acknowledgement
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

matrix_snapshot.title: Readiness review
matrix_snapshot.text: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled repository
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Accidental disclosure
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

matrix_snapshot.title: Respectful conduct
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

matrix_snapshot.title: Knowledge assessment
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

matrix_snapshot.title: Attendance correction
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Version replacement
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Single incident owner
matrix_snapshot.text: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

matrix_snapshot.title: Temporary export removal
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted work
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

matrix_snapshot.title: Manual handling
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

matrix_snapshot.title: Practical competence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

matrix_snapshot.title: Close with evidence
matrix_snapshot.text: The Customer Support Executive must record the resolution, supporting evidence and customer notification before closure. Lack of customer response alone must not be recorded as successful delivery.

matrix_snapshot.title: Recipient verification
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

matrix_snapshot.title: Constructive feedback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled copies
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved fallback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.

matrix_snapshot.title: Open and classify
matrix_snapshot.text: The Customer Support Executive must open a case for each new enquiry, record the shipment ID and classify the issue before advising the customer. Related follow-ups must link to the existing case.

matrix_snapshot.title: Suspicious content
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.

matrix_snapshot.title: Screen lock
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Continuity activation
matrix_snapshot.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.

matrix_snapshot.title: Planned absence notice
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.

matrix_snapshot.title: Non retaliation
matrix_snapshot.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.

matrix_snapshot.title: Emergency evacuation
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.

matrix_snapshot.title: Visitor escort
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.

matrix_snapshot.title: Privacy requests
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.

matrix_snapshot.title: Minimum fallback data
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.

matrix_snapshot.title: Security practice
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted equipment
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must not operate powered warehouse equipment without documented authorization and task-specific training. Observing another operator does not grant authorization.

matrix_snapshot.title: Training retention

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved devices

requirements.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.
requirements.title: Screen lock

requirements.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.
requirements.title: Continuity activation

requirements.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.
requirements.title: Planned absence notice

requirements.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Non retaliation

requirements.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.
requirements.title: Emergency evacuation

requirements.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.
requirements.title: Visitor escort

requirements.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.
requirements.title: Privacy requests

requirements.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.
requirements.title: Minimum fallback data

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.
requirements.title: Security practice

requirements.text: Employees must not operate powered warehouse equipment without documented authorization and task-specific training. Observing another operator does not grant authorization.
requirements.title: Restricted equipment

requirements.text: HR must retain onboarding acknowledgements, assessment attempts and readiness decisions for 24 months after the employee leaves the company, unless a preservation hold applies.
requirements.title: Training retention

requirements.text: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.
requirements.title: Approved devices

requirements.text: Employees must transfer open tasks, critical deadlines and escalation contacts to the designated cover before planned absence. Customer personal data must remain in approved systems.
requirements.title: Shift handover

requirements.text: Employees may propose a simpler fallback step after a rehearsal, provided the proposal preserves privacy, traceability and independent approval.
requirements.title: Continuity improvements

requirements.text: Employees must declare any offered gift valued above PKR 1,000 to HR before accepting it. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited at any value; splitting a gift does not avoid this rule.
requirements.title: Gift declaration

requirements.text: Assigned record owners must reconcile fallback entries within 1 working day of restoration, resolve mismatches and dispose of temporary copies according to POL-06 and POL-07.
requirements.title: Fallback reconciliation

requirements.text: Employees must use fictional or irreversibly anonymized customer examples in training and demonstrations. Replacing a name alone does not anonymize a record containing a real telephone number or address.
requirements.title: Training data

requirements.text: The Customer Support Executive must acknowledge a complaint within 2 working hours of receipt and provide the case reference and next update time. Critical incidents follow POL-09 instead of this routine target.
requirements.title: Acknowledge complaints

requirements.text: Employees must obtain Managing Director approval before representing the company publicly or publishing customer-related material. Personal accounts must not disclose internal records.
requirements.title: Public statements

requirements.text: Employees must record actual events and must not fabricate delivery attempts, training completion, assessment results or approvals. Corrections must retain the original entry and the reason for amendment.
requirements.title: Accurate records

requirements.text: Responders must preserve relevant logs, messages and event identifiers without modifying originals. Evidence access must be restricted to the response team and a preservation hold applied where necessary.
requirements.title: Evidence preservation

requirements.text: Employees must use the confidential HR channel to report misconduct. If the concern involves HR, the report must go directly to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Confidential reporting

requirements.text: Employees must obtain recorded approval before taking planned leave. Submission alone is not approval, and employees must not approve their own request.
requirements.title: Approval before absence

requirements.text: Employees may select an optional development topic after agreeing the time allocation with their manager; optional learning must not delay mandatory training.
requirements.title: Personal development

requirements.text: Employees must transfer personal data only through approved company systems to authorized recipients. Personal messaging accounts and publicly accessible links are prohibited.
requirements.title: Approved transfer

requirements.text: Record owners must retain routine delivery-event records for 180 calendar days after case closure. A documented preservation hold overrides routine deletion until the hold is formally released.
requirements.title: Routine operational retention

requirements.text: Employees must refer records with no applicable retention category to the Operations Manager before deletion. They must not infer a deadline from an unrelated record type.
requirements.title: Retention uncertainty

requirements.text: Teams are encouraged to rehearse one incident scenario each month and document a specific improvement to the response procedure.
requirements.title: Response rehearsal

requirements.text: HR must assign an onboarding plan based on role, experience, location and applicable requirements. Prior experience may change practice difficulty but must not remove mandatory acknowledgements.
requirements.title: Individual plan

requirements.text: Employees must access and collect only the customer fields needed for an assigned task. Full identity documents must not be requested for routine parcel tracking.
requirements.title: Minimum necessary data

requirements.text: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
requirements.title: Incident record

requirements.text: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.
requirements.title: Outage checkpoints

requirements.text: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
requirements.title: Record correction

requirements.text: Employees must pause the affected activity and ask the document owner when two equally authoritative instructions conflict or a necessary limit is missing. The owner must record the resolution before work resumes.
requirements.title: Unclear requirements

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss anticipated leave early so teams can plan coverage before a formal request is submitted.
requirements.title: Calendar planning

requirements.text: Managers must confirm required operational coverage before approving concurrent absences. If coverage cannot be arranged, the manager must record the reason and discuss alternative dates.
requirements.title: Minimum coverage

requirements.text: Employees must activate multifactor authentication before accessing email, remote access or systems holding customer records. IT must provide an approved recovery method rather than disabling the requirement.
requirements.title: Multifactor authentication

requirements.text: Record owners must use approved disposal methods and retain a disposal log identifying category, date range, authorization and completion date. Disposal must not expose readable personal data.
requirements.title: Secure disposal

requirements.text: Employees must disclose a personal or financial relationship with a merchant or supplier before participating in its selection, payment or complaint decision. The manager must assign an independent decision-maker.
requirements.title: Personal interests

requirements.text: The Customer Support Executive must complete approved requester verification before disclosing protected shipment details, following POL-06. A failed verification permits only general public guidance.
requirements.title: Verify the requester

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to suggest improvements to workstation layout or parcel movement after discussing them with the supervisor.
requirements.title: Safety suggestions

requirements.text: Reviewers must verify required evidence before recording completion. Reading a module alone does not demonstrate practical competence or substitute for a required policy acknowledgement.
requirements.title: Completion integrity

requirements.text: Employees must record near misses even when no injury or damage occurs. The supervisor must assign a corrective action owner and verify completion.
requirements.title: Near misses

requirements.text: HR must record each employee role, department, joining date and reporting manager before assigning onboarding. A temporary role change requires a recorded start date, end date and additional requirements.
requirements.title: Role assignment

requirements.text: The Customer Support Executive must check the latest recorded shipment event and applicable SOP before promising a next step. Missing tracking information must be described as unconfirmed.
requirements.title: Use current evidence

requirements.text: The incident lead must obtain an IT health check and an operational sample check before declaring normal service restored. A login screen alone is not evidence of end-to-end recovery.
requirements.title: Recovery verification

requirements.text: Employees must obtain IT approval before installing software or browser extensions on company devices. IT must verify business purpose and permitted access before approval.
requirements.title: Software installation

requirements.text: Employees entering marked warehouse handling zones must wear the posted protective equipment. The supervisor must stop the task if suitable equipment is unavailable.
requirements.title: Personal protective equipment

requirements.text: The Customer Support Executive may propose an FAQ clarification after identifying repeated confusion, subject to owner review before publication.
requirements.title: Improve explanations

requirements.text: Employees must store API keys and service credentials only in approved secret storage and must not include them in source repositories, screenshots, training examples or support tickets.
requirements.title: Secrets handling

requirements.text: Only the incident lead or a designated spokesperson may issue incident updates to merchants or customers. Updates must distinguish confirmed impact from investigation assumptions.
requirements.title: External communication

requirements.text: Employees may suggest removal of unnecessary personal-data fields from forms, reports or dashboards to the relevant process owner.
requirements.title: Privacy improvements

requirements.text: The Customer Support Executive must escalate a routine case still unresolved after 1 working day to the Operations Manager with actions taken and the outstanding decision.
requirements.title: Escalate unresolved work

requirements.text: The Customer Support Executive must send refund requests to the Returns Specialist and must not promise eligibility, amount or payment date before approval under SOP-14 and SOP-16.
requirements.title: Respect refund authority

requirements.text: Employees must classify an incident as critical when it involves immediate physical danger, suspected exposure of customer data or complete loss of dispatch capability. Where severity is uncertain, they must escalate as critical pending review.
requirements.title: Severity classification

requirements.text: Employees must check shipment and transaction identifiers before entering recovered work into the restored system. Potential duplicates must be held for review rather than posted again.
requirements.title: Duplicate prevention

requirements.text: Training managers must distribute learning across Day 1, Week 1, Week 2 and First 30 Days. Mandatory operational deadlines and prerequisites take priority over a convenient stage label.
requirements.title: Learning stages

requirements.text: Employees must report a non-urgent safety concern before the end of the current shift. An immediate danger requires stopping the activity and alerting the shift supervisor at once.
requirements.title: Safety concern reporting

requirements.text: HR must restrict medical or other sensitive absence details to authorized People Operations staff. Operational managers receive only information needed to arrange work.
requirements.title: Sensitive absence details

requirements.text: The Operations Manager must identify scope, owner and start date when issuing a preservation hold. Record owners must suspend scheduled deletion for the named records until written release.
requirements.title: Preservation holds

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to arrange a weekly discussion with an experienced colleague during the first month to clarify workflows and identify useful practice.
requirements.title: Onboarding buddy

requirements.text: The incident lead must record recovery evidence, outstanding risks and corrective action owners before closure. The Operations Manager must review critical incidents within 2 working days after restoration.
requirements.title: Incident closure

requirements.text: Employees must use individually assigned accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Service accounts require a named IT owner and must not be used for routine interactive work.
requirements.title: Individual accounts

requirements.text: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
requirements.title: Authoritative instructions

requirements.text: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
requirements.title: Critical escalation

requirements.text: Employees must complete core orientation within 2 working days of joining. HR must schedule a replacement session within that deadline if the original session is cancelled.
requirements.title: Core orientation
